subject: Control/Data Concord: blueprint alignment + cutover checklist
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai
Cc: cloudops@acme.com
Date: 2028-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy blueprint — one last alignment + cutover window

Logan / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our infra team reviewed the draft blueprint and had a couple of consolidation requests before we lock the cutover window: we want an explicit mapping of which control-plane services will be allowed to egress to Acme-managed telemetry endpoints, and a small appendix describing how KV cache persistence is handled for warm restarts (expected behavior during node replacement).

High level asks: 
- Confirm list of control-plane egress FQDNs/IP ranges and whether mutual TLS is required for metrics/tracing.
- Confirm that the data-plane will be pinned to the tenancy VLAN and will not source egress to customer-managed NFS during the cutover.
- Walk through rollback triggers for a 2-hour cutover window; our SREs want concrete step-by-step safety checks.

Can Redwood share an updated diagram (we drew over your draw.io earlier) and a short cutover checklist spreadsheet that maps owner -> action -> verification step? If we can get that by Tuesday 6/9 EOD PT we can confirm the 6/16 maintenance window.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Platform Engineering Manager, Acme Cloud

Attachments: none (referencing the diagram Logan shared)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy blueprint — one last alignment + cutover window

Sanjay — thanks, this is helpful. Putting the small deliverables below; well iterate quickly and upload an updated diagram + cutover checklist by EOD Tue (6/9).

Quick answers to your asks (well expand in the attachments):
1) Control-plane egress: 3 endpoints (metrics.ingest.redwood.ai, traces.collector.redwood.ai, registry-sync.redwood.ai). All endpoints require mTLS for customer deployments; we will also provide IP ranges for static egress from the control-plane NAT pool.
2) Data-plane egress: data-plane workloads are pinned to the tenant VLAN. By default we block outbound NFS mounts to external customer storage during cutover; if you require NFS, we need a signed exception and a temporary ACL rule.
3) Rollback triggers: we propose three automated triggers (latency > 2x baseline per model pool, error-rate > 1.5% sustained for 5m, failed health-check cascade on >20% of nodes). The checklist includes manual verification steps and whos authorized to flip the rollback play.

Deliverables were attaching: updated draw.io export (controlplane-data-blueprint-v1.drawio.png) and a stub cutover checklist (cutover-checklist.xlsx). See the attached files and the inline diagram notes.

Irene (ops lead) will add the detailed egress CIDRs and mTLS thumbprint expectations; Marissa will enumerate the verification steps per owner; Karthik will confirm KV cache restart semantics and persistence recommendations.

Were aiming to hit Tue EOD — call me if something changes.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Customer Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0182

Attachments: controlplane-data-blueprint-v1.drawio.png, cutover-checklist.xlsx
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>, logan.wright@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-08T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy blueprint — control-plane egress and CIDRs

Sanjay / team,

Following up with the CIDRs and mTLS expectations as promised. Summary (expanded details in the draw.io notes):
- Egress CIDRs (control-plane NAT pool): 35.201.128.0/22, 35.201.132.0/23 (these are static per-region egress addresses we will announce before cutover).
- mTLS: Redwood will present a client cert signed by our CA. For mutual auth, Acme should present a server cert; our collectors will validate SANs and cert expiry. Thumbprint verification is optional — if you prefer we can exchange certs ahead of cutover.

KV cache persistence note (Karthik to expand): by design our inference runtime keeps warm KV caches in ephemeral on-host memory. For warm restarts we persist a compacted checkpoint to a local scratch disk (not NFS) and stream it to the replacement node over the private fabric. That means during node replacement the cache is reconstructed within 30-90s depending on model size. If you require full cold-start avoidance across host failures we can enable a stronger checkpoint cadence but it increases I/O during steady-state.

I'll attach a short table mapping the CIDRs and egress hostnames to the diagram layers.

Irene
Head of Field Ops | Redwood Inference

Attachment: egress-cidrs-table (embedded in draw.io export)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>, logan.wright@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-08T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy blueprint — cutover checklist draft

Sanjay / Logan — attaching the checklist draft (cutover-checklist.xlsx). Key items called out here that we want Acme to verify ahead of the window:
- Network ACLs: control-plane NAT pool CIDRs allowed to metrics/tracing endpoints (owner: Acme Netops).
- TLS handshake smoke test: mutual auth test 5m pre-cutover (owner: Redwood Field Ops).
- KV cache health baseline: observe two baseline test runs and record cold/warm latencies (owner: Acme SRE + Redwood runbooks).
- Rollback manual gate: approved personnel list (owner: Acme SRE) — we will not execute automated rollback without a manual confirmation for the first cutover.

One small ask: can Acme provide a short list of test tenants (3 example tenants) and a sample request pattern we can use for baseline collection? That will let us finalize the latency thresholds in the checklist.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: cutover-checklist.xlsx
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-09T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy blueprint — confirming delivery and next steps

Team — this looks good. Weve provisioned an internal playbook slot to validate the mTLS handshake and smoke test on 6/13; SREs will upload the sample tenant patterns to the Drive link you shared by EOD 6/10. Two quick clarifications:
1) For KV cache persistence: do you have a recommended scratch-disk sizing guideline per model size? Our ops lead asked for an explicit Sizing table so were not under-provisioning.
2) For rollback: we accept the manual gate for the first cutover. Can you add a short contact list with on-call rotations for anyone authorized to approve rollback?

If you can add those to the checklist and re-upload well greenlight the 6/16 window. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Sanjay
Platform Engineering Manager, Acme Cloud
